text: Hack the Hub on the Commons Hub server: participants open the prepared graph, get an account automatically and propose their own graphs
description:
Felix 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12, for the Hack the Hub event at Commons Hub:
- The two organizers prepare an idea graph that gives a rough structure of what could be done.
- Participants open it without a login, read ideas and find things they can work on.
- It must be extraordinarily simple: an account is created automatically with a key in the browser.
- A participant who wants to build something drags from an idea into empty space, creates their own graph and offers it to that idea; the organizers accept.
- Participants can leave notes on ideas (34b3d747).

This is the first slice of "people own graphs" (d4203221) on one server, without links across servers.

What it needs from the build: many graphs on one server, accounts with automatic login, access per graph, proposing with offer and acceptance, and the safety limits. What remains after the build is deployment on the Commons Hub server and preparing the graph, both for Felix and the co-organizer.

Not known to Claude: the date of the event.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Participants need a place for their own graph next to the prepared one.
An account without a form lets participants act within seconds.
supportingConnections.reflection: 2026-11-13: creating a graph or leaving a note needs no form in the tests; the time it takes a participant is not measured, nobody has tried it.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: The organizers keep control of the prepared graph while participants own theirs.
supportingConnections.reflection: 2026-11-13: in the tests an account without rights cannot change the organizers' graph and owns the graphs it creates. Not yet tried with the organizers and participants.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Offering a graph to an idea is how participants say what they will work on.
supportingConnections.reflection: Ready for the event: offering, accepting and editing the offered space in place work, including value display and undo. Whether participants use offers to say what they will work on is only known after Hack the Hub.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: The server can be opened to all participants without risk.
supportingConnections.reflection: Holds as far as tests show; the event itself is the first real load.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Notes let participants ask questions and show interest without creating a graph.
supportingConnections.reflection: Ready, untested with participants: notes and interest need no graph of one's own; the event will show whether people use them.

status.comment:
2026-11-22: everything the event needs is built: many graphs per server (548c5b94), automatic accounts (383e8949), access per graph (8faf6a70), notes (34b3d747), offering a graph to an idea and accepting it (b7e0b972, implemented today), safety limits incl. graph size (8a303626). Checked read-only on https://ideas.commons-hub.at: login accounts, signUp open + browserKey, offers procedure answers, spaces 'ideas' (22 ideas, has 'hack the hub!') and 'aimparency'.

Waiting on Felix (server access), checklist:
1. On the server (/srv/aimparency/aimparency, user aimparency): git pull && sudo systemctl restart aimparency (pnpm start rebuilds), so today's fixes are live (space handover 342efe11, size limit eab65397/4e48c7f1, in-place value + undo b5e26039/d4b92ad0). Watch journalctl -u aimparency -f for a clean start.
2. server.json: check "graphCreation": "everyone" so participants' automatic accounts can create their own graph; keep limits (graphsPerAccount 20, graphMegabytes 50).
3. Prepare the graph: either a new space 'Hack the Hub' or the 'hack the hub!' idea in 'ideas' with the challenges as sub-ideas, each with a short description; set its notes to 'everyone' in the space settings.
4. Dry run with a second browser (private window): open the space link, drag out of a challenge into empty space, 'Propose a space' → new space, then accept it as owner. Then undo an edit inside the offered space.
5. Put the space link (https://ideas.commons-hub.at/spaces/<slug>) on the event page or a QR code.
Only question: which of step 3's two options (own space vs. inside 'ideas')?
